key_insight: Gravity and particle inertia jointly reshape clustering in cylinder wakes, transforming particle voids and clusters through a settling-dominated parameter St/Fr^2.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and control particle dispersion, deposition, and slip behavior in bluff-body flows relevant to multiphase transport and sedimenting aerosols.
method: Direct numerical simulation of particle-laden flow over a cylinder
Cases at Re = 100 and 200 with varied Stokes number, particle loading, and Froude number
Voronoi statistics combined with local Q-criterion to quantify clustering and voids
evidence_signal: The abstract reports Reynolds-number-dependent wake recovery and a systematic evolution of void shapes and Voronoi cell-area distributions across particle inertia and gravity settings.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on simulated unbounded vertical-channel cylinder wakes, so extrapolation to complex geometries or dense particle suspensions may require additional validation.
paper_title: Role of gravity on preferential clustering of microparticles in unsteady wake flows
